method: Complete unobfuscated source and call/flow facts reviewed; no external feed, scanner conviction or advisory used as verdict evidence.

scan_compatibility.issue: Installed atomscan embeds an older Cleave rejecting the already-reviewed metadata/file/naming budget of 101.
scan_compatibility.adapter: Scanned an isolated copy of the rules from its own working directory, omitting only metadata/file/naming::filename-msedge-substring. It has no exact consumers and cannot match any submitted basename. The real repository rule was preserved.
scan_compatibility.verification: Every final trait ID, criticality and description from the adapter exactly equals the full current-engine scan on the unmodified complete working rule tree for each submitted file.
scan_compatibility.model_limit: Installed model v18.18 warns that its feature spec is v18 while the extractor produces v19. Scores are recorded, not treated as behavioral evidence.

corrections: Bare paths, hardcoded Telegram URL syntax, form-value reads, field/key context, and local page-routing mechanics moved out of attacker-objective namespaces. Exact consumers follow the new IDs.

Payment/login/OTP fields plus form-value reads and a page-command route map alone do not prove an attack or security-boundary crossing. These and local map/index/navigation co-occurrence are now notable. The ordinary checkout control matched the three former suspicious observations and contains no capture/transfer behavior.
Complete form-value reads and browser navigation are notable rather than component. Partial OTP/key context remains component.
Inherited phishing/exfiltration ATT&CK and MBC mappings were removed from the moved neutral observations.

The former operator-flow population is retained as browser-page-routed-sensitive-input-collection, including HTML; a tested HTML control preserves its capture finding. Actual operator steering now additionally requires a bound WebSocket receiver, parsed message command, guarded table index and the same command/table supplying location navigation. No required endpoint or chosen session identifier is used.

Neutral path relocations also activate truthful generic credential-path and resource-read observations through existing directory consumers; no hostile consumer was artificially restored using neutral atoms.

tests.result: 11 controls passed. Existing first-party token refresh remains nonhostile; third-party token theft and three existing Rust credential-exfiltration fixtures retain attack coverage. Local checkout loses three unsupported suspicious findings. Renamed phishing source retains capture and gains bound steering. An unrelated navigation lookup rejects bound steering. HTML capture remains covered.

material_detection_losses: None on the three submitted sources or existing attack controls after relocation/rename normalization. Three ordinary-checkout suspicious observations are correctly notable. Old HTML/local-routing capture population is retained under an honest name.

samples.marker_line: Docker sender: registry credentials enter a Telegram POST
samples.identity: Minimal Rust Docker-credential sender; byte-identical to the repository simple-stealer fixture.
execution: main resolves the home directory and reads .docker/config.json into a byte vector; read errors become an empty vector.

The same byte vector is passed to reqwest blocking POST.body and send at a hardcoded Telegram sendMessage URL; the response is ignored. No shell, privilege change, persistence, encryption, or additional payload exists.
limits: The bot secret is explicitly example-like; the request has no chat_id or text fields. This establishes an attempted raw credential-body transfer, not successful delivery into an attacker-readable chat.

The complete manifest, dependencies, deployment trigger, authorization, and original package context are unavailable. Source test-fixture appearance weakens confidence but does not change the explicit credential-grab-and-send purpose.
samples.evidence_tipping_verdict: The sole useful operation reads registry authentication material and puts it directly into an unrelated chat-service request, without any registry authentication or user-facing management operation.
samples.coverage_gap: Only one distinct hostile chain is supported. The retained hostile credential export and suspicious token-shaped URL are not inflated into multiple hostile detections to satisfy a count.

samples.marker_line: Outsider client: login/card/OTP capture and remote page control
samples.identity: Outsider/JWR-style live browser phishing client; family-compatible configuration and session-key markers are present.
execution: Top-level code creates a persistent session ID, a WebSocket, and a Web Worker.

A capture-phase document input listener copies selected username, password, card number, expiry, CVV and OTP fields into one record on every edit; it posts the complete plaintext record to the worker.
The record is JSON-serialized and encrypted with a freshly generated 32-byte AES-CTR key and 16-byte counter; only the returned ciphertext is sent over the socket.
A socket message is JSON-parsed; its command selects one of four page routes, guarded by a table lookup, then drives location.assign. Unknown commands do nothing.
Campaign appearance fields and the post-error address are declared configuration only; the supplied code never uses them to render or redirect.
limits: The WebSocket hostname uses .invalid; no live server is demonstrated. The worker body and HTML pages are absent.

The AES key and counter are never transmitted or retained for the receiver, so this source does not demonstrate a decryptable server-side credential stream. Worker plaintext forwarding is directly implemented.
localStorage.getItem runs before the try block, and socket.send has no readiness check; execution can fail in restrictive storage contexts or before socket connection.
samples.evidence_tipping_verdict: Continuous collection of login secrets, payment details and OTP values, a plaintext worker handoff and remote steering of payment/challenge pages together support phishing rather than ordinary form submission.
samples.coverage_gap: Capture, worker forwarding, encrypted transmission and now bound operator page steering are covered. No successful MFA bypass or server-side decryption is claimed.

samples.marker_line: Agent collector: cross-vendor auth-store sweep; no upload
samples.identity: Standalone Go cross-vendor AI-agent store collector.
execution: main invokes collectAgentStores. A fixed twelve-path catalog targets Claude, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini and Kiro stores.
Each rule is passed through os.ExpandEnv; leading tilde-plus-backslash is stripped and the remainder joined under os.UserHomeDir.
os.ReadFile is attempted for each resulting path. Successful contents are appended unmodified to a local byte-slice collection and returned; main discards the result.
There is no network API, output/write, persistence, decryption, privilege operation, or secondary execution path.
limits: Go os.ExpandEnv does not expand percent-delimited APPDATA. Backslashes remain literal filename characters on Unix; most intended nested store paths therefore do not resolve there. The top-level .claude.json path does resolve normally.
Windows would interpret the post-tilde backslashes as separators, but the percent-APPDATA entries remain defective. Runtime acquisition was not claimed for any real credential file.

An authorized backup/import integration is possible in a larger unseen project. The supplied executable has no migration, refresh, user-selected source, or other functional purpose beyond gathering stores, and provides no authorization context.
samples.evidence_tipping_verdict: The intentionally broad authentication-store target list feeding a collection named loot, with no use by the corresponding applications, supports a credential-harvesting component. Verdict confidence is lower than for a complete exfiltration chain.
samples.coverage_gap: Three retained hostile catalog detections describe overlapping authentication/configuration collection evidence. They do not establish exfiltration or three separate hostile routines.

classifier_disagreements: Rust remains SUSPICIOUS and Go remains BENIGN despite the reviewed malicious credential-send/collection purposes. JavaScript remains HOSTILE. No inaccurate objective atom or duplicate hostile behavior was restored to alter those scores.
